title: Lincoln: The Two-Minute Speech That Redefined America

lines: A speech of just two minutes changed how America saw itself.
Who changed the world today? November 19.
Who changed the world today? November nineteenth.
163 years ago today,
One hundred sixty-three years ago today,
at a new cemetery in Pennsylvania,
President Abraham Lincoln gave the Gettysburg Address.

lines: In July 1863, the American Civil War was at its fiercest.
In July eighteen sixty-three, the American Civil War was at its fiercest.
For three days, two armies fought at Gettysburg,
For three days, two armies fought around the small town of Gettysburg,
and more than fifty thousand men were killed, wounded, or missing.
Thousands of fallen soldiers were buried on the hillside nearby.

lines: On November 19, the new national cemetery was dedicated.
On November nineteenth, the new national cemetery was dedicated.
The main speaker, Edward Everett, talked for two full hours.
Then Lincoln stood up,
and spoke for about two minutes, fewer than three hundred words.

scenes.chapter: Chapter 3  Of the people, by the people
lines: He said the nation believed all men are created equal,
He said the nation was born believing that all men are created equal,
that these dead must not have died in vain,
that the nation shall have a new birth of freedom,
that government of, by and for the people shall not perish.
and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.
He said the world would little note what was said there,
yet the speech became one of the most famous in history.
In April 1865, soon after the war ended, he was assassinated,
In April eighteen sixty-five, soon after the war ended, he was assassinated,
at the age of fifty-six.
Great words do not have to be long,
and in two minutes, he put a nation's ideals into words.
His question for you:
If you had only two minutes, what is the one thing you would say?
